blocks.raw: A Webhook, in simple terms, is a user-defined HTTP callback. It is a mechanism for the system to notify you about an event. How does it notify you? By doing an HTTP POST to the Webhook (i.e. the Web URL that you define). In terms of implementation, you can write an API endpoint that is capable of receiving an HTTP POST in an application stack of your choice.
blocks.text: A Webhook, in simple terms, is a user-defined HTTP callback. It is a mechanism for the system to notify you about an event. How does it notify you? By doing an HTTP POST to the Webhook (i.e. the Web URL that you define). In terms of implementation, you can write an API endpoint that is capable of receiving an HTTP POST in an application stack of your choice.

blocks.raw: Remember in live this must be reliable and resilient if you are to depend on it for information.
blocks.text: Remember in live this must be reliable and resilient if you are to depend on it for information.

blocks.raw: The advantage of a Webhook is that there is no persistent open connection to the system where you keep filtering for events that you are interested in. It is an asynchronous mechanism where you will wait for the system to notify you. The HTTP POST payload will contain the details of the event.

blocks.raw: We sign the POST request with an HMAC digest, using a secret that you provide. This can be set when registering the endpoint for the webhook type of notification. It is required that you validate this signature, particularly if you are acting upon these events to authorise actions in your system. The method of calculation of the hmac signature is the same as in HMAC Signatures / Authorisation header calculation
